title: The assignment and the user experience
subtitle: What problem the product must solve, what the demonstration must prove, and which boundaries matter.
purpose: Help a person recover useful work history and apply it to a present request, with evidence and effortless control. The leading recurring task still needs to be selected.

steps.title: Choose a useful task
steps.body: Start from a recurring user need. Select the few capabilities that create meaningful value; memory capacity alone is not a product.

steps.title: Ground it in history
steps.body: Use real persisted transcripts and model decisions. Recover relevant facts, preferences and episodes, including information distributed across records.

steps.title: Show changed behavior
steps.body: A later answer or draft should use supported context. Make uncertainty, corrections and forgetting understandable in ordinary use.

steps.title: Prove the experience
steps.body: Demonstrate the real interface and backend, then evaluate the complete pipeline and let a reviewer import unfamiliar history.

panels.title: Two coherent modes
items: Regular dictation preserves intended content; vocabulary and writing style are separate concerns.
Hey Kivi uses relevant history for interactive help. Memory does not authorize unsolicited content insertion.
Transcript replay and typed requests are acceptable. Speech recognition and production Kivi integration are not required.

panels.title: Independent product work
items: First use Kivi and study other products: how memory, personalization and user control relate.
Part One: applicant forms and writes a position of at most 100 words and a vision of at most 600 words.
The brief excludes generative AI from arriving at or writing Part One. Preserve both documents before Part Two.
This technical SVG pack is AI-assisted planning material. It is not the applicant's Part One submission.

panels.title: A complete demonstration
items: A normal-user interface must begin and end the experience; a CLI is only an intermediate build milestone.
Narrow tools are acceptable; history questions cannot be restricted to a memorized demonstration script.
Supported recall, useful context, uncertainty, control and inspectable sources must work together.

example: Illustrative journey, not the final product choice: recall the Jaipur budget → draft a checklist → change the budget → inspect its source → forget it → verify the next answer respects that change.
remaining: Select the first recurring task, confirm the applicant's Part One status, and specify normal, ambiguous, corrected, forgotten and failed outcomes. The working interface/backend are not built.
mentor_question: Does the chosen recurring task create enough value to justify what this product remembers?

title: Import history without losing its meaning
subtitle: The durable source ledger is the starting evidence for both search and learning.
purpose: Accept paired transcript records from development data or a reviewer's corpus. Preserve original evidence, missing metadata and source identity before deriving memories.

steps.title: Validate the envelope
steps.body: Read raw ASR, formatted text, source identity and available metadata. Keep optional times, app and project fields missing when unknown.

steps.title: Resolve import identity
steps.body: Use stable record ID, revision and payload. Repeating an import must not duplicate an event; identical text can still describe distinct events.

steps.title: Commit source and jobs
steps.body: Persist the original revision and head, permitted visibility and required durable work in one transaction. Record each row's outcome.

steps.title: Expose permitted search
steps.body: Make allowed source text searchable independently of extraction. Queue learning and optional encoding with visible stage readiness and failures.

panels.title: Proposed import contract
items: schema_version; record_id and revision; exact raw_asr and formatted_text.
Optional captured_at, timezone and available_at preserve distinct meanings.
Optional app, conversation_id, project_id and original metadata; app name is not project identity.
Trusted user scope comes from the application/import command, not from the model or an arbitrary row.

panels.title: Evidence rules
items: Raw and formatted text are paired versions of one observation, not independent corroboration.
Preserve material disagreement; fluent formatting does not establish factual truth.
Evidence spans use original field/revision and zero-based Unicode character positions, with end excluded.
Normalization, transliteration or chunking needs a mapping back to original spans.

panels.title: Integrity and reviewer use
items: Account for every row: accepted, duplicate, pending or rejected, with a reason.
Restart/resume must retain progress. An empty extraction is different from a processing failure.
Reimport cannot silently recreate excluded or deleted knowledge; define explicit restoration separately.
Document import, process, inspect, query and reset for another approximately 500-record corpus.

example: An old transcript imported today can describe last month's budget. Its arrival time must not make that old value overwrite a supported newer budget. Missing source dates remain unknown.
remaining: Freeze and implement the import schema, migrations, source inspection, keyword indexing, durable jobs and reset behavior. Create a small reviewed fixture before expanding to the full corpus.
mentor_question: Can a reviewer import ordinary logs without inventing metadata or repairing undocumented setup?
terms: Revision = a specific saved version. Head = the selected current revision. Permitted projection = only the source text still eligible for use. A span identifies an exact passage in the original text.

title: What a memory contains and how it is stored
subtitle: One SQLite database holds source evidence, versioned interpretations and independent search representations.
purpose: A memory is an attributed claim with evidence and qualified applicability. Twelve content labels organize shared records; they do not create twelve databases or isolated retrieval routes.

steps.title: Source evidence
steps.body: Preserve original text and metadata under a source revision. Current permitted projections govern how this evidence can be used.

steps.title: Supported interpretation
steps.body: Store subject, predicate, typed value, units, scope, time, attribution, modality, evidence and lifecycle. Keep prior revisions and accepted decisions.

steps.title: Independent indexes
steps.body: Index allowed sources even when no memory is admitted. Build memory keyword/vector indexes separately; record revisions, configuration and readiness.

panels.title: Core schema contracts
items: Memory form: semantic knowledge, episodic experience or a user-authorized reusable procedure.
Separate direct statement, tool observation, inference and summary; derived material retains its dependencies.
Evidence links exact memory/source revisions and spans. Scope and time qualify the claim.
Source/memory heads, aliases/edges, exclusions, jobs, operation receipts and owner revisions preserve lifecycle and auditability.

panels.title: Content labels 1–6
items: 1. Entities and attributes: people, organizations, equipment and stated capabilities.
2. Relationships and roles: family, teams, ownership and responsibility.
3. Preferences and priorities: likes, style and contextual tradeoffs.
4. Constraints and requirements: budgets, units, limits and conditions.
5. Routines and recurring patterns: supported regular behavior.
6. Goals and desired outcomes: aspirations, separate from promises.

panels.title: Content labels 7–12
items: 7. Plans, tasks and commitments: distinct intention and obligation types.
8. Decisions and stated reasons: accepted choices; preserve reasons only when stated.
9. Progress, blockers and issues: task state, dependencies and questions.
10. Beliefs, ideas and hypotheses: attributed thought, not confirmed truth.
11. Personal vocabulary: what a term refers to or means.
12. Resources and references: files, links and locations; no implied access.

example: “For the Jaipur trip, our total hotel budget is INR 6,000” → category: constraint; value: 6000; currency: INR; scope: Jaipur trip; meaning: total hotel budget; evidence: exact phrase. It does not imply INR 6,000 per night.
remaining: Implement actual SQL constraints, migrations, predicate rules and evidence mappings. The schema is currently a reviewed logical contract; no product database implementation exists.
mentor_question: Which structured fields are essential to reliable behavior, and which can wait for demonstrated value?
terms: Predicate = the relationship or property being asserted. Modality = fact, intention, belief or condition. Polarity = positive or negated meaning. Head = current selected version; older versions retain their history.

title: Make memory understandable in the application
subtitle: The person gets useful help and simple controls; an engineer can inspect the underlying decision.
purpose: Connect the final normal-user interface to the same MemoryService as the CLI. Memory should improve the task without requiring the user to administer records or graph nodes.

steps.title: Ask naturally
steps.body: Enter a Hey Kivi request or replay transcript history. Show processing state and allow cancellation; native speech capture is optional.

steps.title: Receive a useful result
steps.body: Present a supported answer, draft, clarification or honest partial outcome. Apply current instructions and relevant remembered context.

steps.title: Inspect the evidence
steps.body: Open the source interactions that support personal claims. Distinguish source text, learned interpretation, uncertainty and actual tool observations.

steps.title: Correct or forget
steps.body: Offer simple natural controls and an explicit targeted path. Acknowledge success only after the backend commits the change.

steps.title: See future behavior change
steps.body: A later request should respect corrected values and exclusions. Reconnect/replay must not return a stale forbidden answer.

panels.title: Normal-user surfaces
items: Question and answer with usable sources, without exposing database jargon.
Ambiguity: one focused question or supported alternatives; skipping preserves uncertainty.
Remember/correct/forget and source deletion with clear retention wording.
Visible pending, unsaved, cancelled, failed and unknown outcomes; no invented completion.

panels.title: Engineer inspection
items: Input → created/changed/rejected memory → retrieved evidence → resulting behavior.
Show exact source revisions/spans, relevant memory state, policy/configuration versions and concise decision reasons.
Expose stage readiness, worker failures, retries, model usage, latency and cost basis.
The same permission/exclusion boundary applies to retained trace content and source inspection.

panels.title: Experience acceptance
items: Recall and changed-state answers work through the actual UI and persistent backend.
Correction, forgetting, ambiguous references and partial failures have coherent user-visible outcomes.
The final product must be intelligible without a developer console or an explanation of the storage system.
CLI and interface use one core implementation. The frontend/API framework remains undecided.

example: User: “Why did you choose that budget?” → show the original update. User: “That was for Goa.” → resolve scope, commit the correction, and give the next Jaipur answer from the corrected permitted history.
remaining: Select the concrete journey, frontend and application adapter. Build the answer/evidence/control experience and exercise it against real persisted state. No final user interface currently exists.
mentor_question: Can someone verify and correct a result without becoming the administrator of the memory system?

title: Prove quality with a reproducible evaluation
subtitle: Measure the complete product and compare added memory against simpler source-based approaches.
purpose: Show where the system succeeds, abstains and fails. Use human-reviewed evidence and held-out cases to test generalization to unfamiliar dictation history.

steps.title: Build realistic history
steps.body: Create about 500 paired records: recurring people/events, distractors, changed facts, missing metadata, ASR disagreements and multilingual cases.

steps.title: Review questions and evidence
steps.body: Propose 80 questions: 30 development, 50 sealed. Separately audit 50 source records. Keep gold answers and labels out of ingestion.

steps.title: Compare complete pipelines
steps.body: Hold answer model, instructions, scope and cutoffs constant. Compare full history, source keyword, source hybrid and hybrid with typed memories.

steps.title: Diagnose before tuning
steps.body: Inspect admission, retrieval, evidence packing, answer support, controls and tools. Change one justified component using development failures.

steps.title: Freeze and report
steps.body: Freeze the candidate before sealed evaluation. Retain failures, denominators, traces and costs; rehearse the reviewer path on the submitted code.

panels.title: Cases and leakage control
items: Cover direct recall, multi-record evidence, time/changes, insufficient/conflicted history and contextual assistance.
Proposed sealed split: 40 answerable + 10 insufficient/conflicting cases; source audit split: 20 development + 30 sealed.
Separate whole narratives/templates; evaluate only records available at the query cutoff and allowed by current exclusions.
Test English, Hindi/Hinglish, cross-language queries, names, negation and ambiguous dates. Hidden-corpus languages remain unknown.
Give the full-history baseline all permitted context when it fits; disclose truncation and compare availability fairly.

panels.title: Quality and integrity
items: Measure fully supported task success: required content, correct subject/time and no material unsupported additions.
Audit admission precision/recall, all-required-evidence coverage, citations, false abstention and inappropriate personalization.
Test source fallback, corrections, forgetting, stale jobs/answers, cross-user scope, hostile history and actual tool outcomes.
Proposed gates: ≥95% admitted precision; ≥80% eligible recall; ≥34/40 supported answers; ≥9/10 correct insufficient-history fallbacks.
Critical failures must be zero: wrong-person or invented-authority writes, cross-user or excluded-content release, and false success.

panels.title: Operations and honest claims
items: Report retrieval and full-response latency, cold starts, failures, indexing lag, database/model size, calls, tokens and cost basis.
Proposed targets: warm retrieval p95 ≤500 ms; full response p50 ≤5 s / p95 ≤15 s. None is measured yet.
Proposed budget: 320 reader attempts; extraction, encoding and judging have separate budgets. An exhausted run is incomplete.
Only the isolated storage probe has passed 12/12. Product quality, real concurrency, recovery and performance remain untested.

example: A fluent answer with the wrong person's budget fails. So does a correct number supported by the wrong source, a historical value presented as current, or an answer that recovers forgotten information.
remaining: Build corpus, annotations, baselines, integrity tests and results. Proposed complexity gate: ≥3 net added successes/50, or preserved quality with ≥20% lower p95 latency or intended-horizon cost; no critical or temporal regression. Small differences may be inconclusive.
mentor_question: What evidence would convince us that structured memory improves the task enough to justify its errors and cost?

title: Make the complete product reproducible
subtitle: A reviewing agent will clone the final commit, follow RUN.md, import new history and evaluate the actual system.
purpose: Eliminate undocumented setup and demonstration-only behavior. The proposed primary arrangement is a local application/database connected to a hosted model API.

steps.title: Install and configure
steps.body: Declare runtimes, versions, dependency commands and every environment variable. Provide an environment example with no credentials committed.

steps.title: Create and start
steps.body: Provide exact commands to create, migrate and seed the database, start required processes, and open the user interface.

steps.title: Operate and inspect
steps.body: Explain primary interactions, memory/source inspection and meaningful limitations. The reviewer should use the product without repairing setup.

steps.title: Import and evaluate
steps.body: Document another-corpus translation/import, processing, history-grounded queries, evaluation command and the location of results and memory state.

steps.title: Reset and rehearse
steps.body: Document a bounded reset. Test the complete install/start/import/process/operate/inspect/evaluate/reset path from the submitted commit.

panels.title: Repository deliverables
items: Applicant's independently authored position and vision, with the brief's required ordering.
Complete source code, a working normal-user interface and a real connected backend.
Database schema/migrations, reproducible seed data and the approximately 500-record corpus.
Runnable evaluation, generated results, visible failures, limitations and inspectable decision traces.

panels.title: README and RUN.md
items: README explains product, architecture, use cases, limitations, results and actual AI use.
RUN.md begins with the primary review method, then lists all setup, database and process commands.
Include interface location, interactions, evaluation command, new-corpus procedure, inspection locations and reset instructions.
Name credentials precisely, pin required versions, and disclose model-download/startup needs. No private credentials in Git.

panels.title: Reviewer and submission boundary
items: The reviewer may supply documented credentials and translate its own roughly 500 dictations into the declared import format.
It will not infer missing steps, perform undocumented dashboard work, repair the application or ask for clarification.
Submit one repository URL and the exact final commit SHA. Add the application URL when hosted is the primary method.
Hosting and Docker are optional. A hosted review path additionally needs a direct URL, access details and complete operating instructions.

example: A successful rehearsal starts from a clean checkout, creates fresh state, imports an unfamiliar fixture, asks a supported history question, inspects its sources, runs evaluation and resets without hidden manual work.
remaining: Implement the product and document commands only after testing them. RUN.md, actual migrations, seed data, corpus and evaluation results are still required deliverables.
mentor_question: Could a new reviewer reproduce the claimed behavior using only this repository and declared credentials?

title: From reviewed plan to a complete product
subtitle: Use mentor feedback to narrow the first useful journey and turn each milestone into observable evidence.
purpose: Preserve the core truth and control guarantees while building the smallest complete path. Planning coverage is not a measure of implemented product completion.

steps.title: Specify the first journey
steps.body: Select one recurring task and its normal, ambiguous, changed, forgotten and failed states. Account for independently authored Part One.

steps.title: Persist and inspect sources
steps.body: Build import, migrations, source identity, permitted projections, inspection and keyword search. Prove restart/reimport and relevant scope/exclusion rules.

steps.title: Complete one answer path
steps.body: Connect the model/coordinator to persisted sources. Add citations, honest unknowns, explicit controls and measured calls/latency.

steps.title: Add measured memory
steps.body: Implement selective extraction, temporal/entity handling and source fallback. Test optional embeddings and relationship expansion against simpler baselines.

steps.title: Finish the experience
steps.body: Connect the normal-user interface and one justified artifact tool to the same core. Exercise evidence, control and failure states.

steps.title: Evaluate and rehearse
steps.body: Freeze the pipeline, run sealed comparisons, report failures and costs, and complete the clean-checkout reviewer procedure.

panels.title: What exists now
items: Canonical architecture, research dossier, process guide and these explanatory diagrams.
An executable research-only SQLite contract experiment with 12/12 checks recorded as passing.
The probe does not validate real concurrency, disk recovery, model meaning, graph cleanup, external tools or speed.

panels.title: What remains open
items: First recurring journey; final UI/API framework; admission, sensitive-data and retention experience.
Exact DeepSeek endpoint/output behavior; embedding default; multilingual accuracy, cost and latency.
Actual application, CLI, schema/migrations, corpus, live model integration and product evaluation are unbuilt.
Quality thresholds and performance targets are proposals to test, not achieved promises.

panels.title: Decisions to discuss with a mentor
items: Is the chosen task useful enough, and is its memory scope defensible?
Are evidence, changes, ambiguity and forgetting understandable to the user?
Which baseline proves benefit, and what failure would change the design?
What should be cut? Defer graph servers, Redis, answer caches, autonomous reflection and broad integrations until justified.

example: First engineering success: a small reviewed history survives restart; a real query returns a cited answer; a correction changes the next answer; forgetting blocks the same information through source search and replay.
remaining: The next recommended deliverable is a small behavior specification and acceptance cases. Build source persistence and a cited-answer path next, with evaluation fixtures alongside implementation.
mentor_question: Which three observations would tell us this first end-to-end slice is ready to expand?
